title: Complete 95-Generation Synchronized Puranic Royal & Rishi Genealogies of India (F.E. Pargiter, Ancient Indian Historical Tradition, 1922)

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine (Gens 2–30): Ikshvaku → Vikukshi → Kakutstha → Yuvanashva I → Shravasta → Kuvalashva → Yuvanashva II → Mandhatri → Purukutsa → Trasadasyu → Trayyaruna
nodes.era: Satya Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 2-30, p. 145)
nodes.role: First 30 Generations of the Solar Dynasty of Ayodhya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 90-92, 145
nodes.notes: Complete early Aikshvaku kings: Shravasta founded Shravasti; Emperor Mandhatri (Gen 21) conquered the Pauravas & Druhyus; son Purukutsa married Narmada; grandson Trasadasyu is celebrated in the Rigveda!

nodes.name: Ayodhya Solar Spine (Gens 31–64): Trishanku → Harishchandra → Rohita → Bahu → Sagara → Asamanjas → Amshumant → Bhagiratha → Ambarisha → Rituparna → Kalmashapada → Dilipa II → Raghu → Aja → Dasharatha
nodes.era: Treta Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 31-64, pp. 145, 147)
nodes.role: Golden Era of the Solar Dynasty Leading to Lord Rama
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 92-94, 145-147
nodes.notes: Satyavrata-Trishanku & truthful King Harishchandra (Gen 32); Emperor Sagara (Gen 41, destroyed the Haihaya raiders!); Bhagiratha (Gen 45, brought the Ganges to earth); Rituparna (Gen 51, host of Nala!); Dilipa II -> Raghu -> Aja -> Dasharatha (Gen 64).

nodes.name: Ayodhya Post-Rama Spine (Gens 66–95): Kusha → Atithi → Nishadha → Nala → Hiranyanabha (Yoga Master!) → Pushya → Agnivarna → Maru → Brihadbala (Slain at Kurukshetra) → Brihatkshaya
nodes.era: Dvapara Yuga (Pargiter Master Table Gens 66-95, p. 149)
nodes.role: 30 Generations from Rama's Son Kusha to the Mahabharata War
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 94-95, 149
nodes.notes: Complete post-Rama Solar kings down to Gen 94 King Brihadbala of Kosala (slain by Arjuna's son Abhimanyu at the Bharata Battle, c. 950 BCE!) and continuing via Divakara to the Shakya clan of Gautama Buddha!

nodes.name: Videha / Mithila Solar Dynasty (All 54 Kings): Nimi → Mithi Janaka → Udavasu → Hrasvaroman → Siradhvaja Janaka (Father of Sita!) & Kushadhvaja → Bahulashva → Kritakshana → Janaka-Ugrasena
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 95-96, 145-149
nodes.notes: Founded by Ikshvaku's son Nimi -> Mithi Janaka (founder of Mithila). Siradhvaja Janaka (Gen 64, contemporary of Dasharatha) discovered Goddess Sita; post-battle Janaka-Ugrasena & Janaka-Dharmadhvaja appear in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad with sage Yajnavalkya!

nodes.name: Manu's Other Solar Kingdoms: Vaisali (Nabhanedishtha → Bhalandana → Marutta → Trinabindu → Vishala → Pramati), Sharyatas (Anarta/Dvaraka → Raivata Kakudmin) & Nabhagas (Ambarisha → Rathitara)
nodes.role: Ancient Dynasties of North Bihar (Vaisali) & Gujarat (Anarta)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 97-98, 145-147
nodes.notes: Nabhanedishtha's line produced Emperor Marutta (Gen 40), Trinabindu (whose daughter Ilavila married Rishi Pulastya -> Vishravas -> Kubera & Ravana!), and Vishala (founder of Vaisali). Sharyati's line ruled Anarta (Gujarat), whose princess Revati married Balarama!

nodes.name: Kanyakubja Dynasty (Amavasu Line): Amavasu → Bhima → Jahnu → Kusha → Kushika → King Gadhi → Vishvamitra (Kshatriya-Turned-Brahmarshi!) → Ashtaka → Lauhi
nodes.role: Aila Kingdom of Kanauj & Origin of the Gayatri Mantra Rishi Vishvamitra
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 99-101, 234-237
nodes.notes: Pururavas's second son Amavasu founded Kanyakubja -> Jahnu (adopted River Ganga as 'Jahnavi') -> Gadhi (whose daughter Satyavati married Bhargava Richika -> Jamadagni -> Parashurama!) -> Vishvaratha-Vishvamitra (composer of Rigveda Mandala III & Gayatri Mantra; adopted Shunahshepa-Devarata!).

nodes.name: Kasi (Varanasi) Dynasty: Kshatravriddha → Sunahotra → Kasha → Dhanvantari (Father of Ayurveda!) → Divodasa I & II → Pratardana → Alarka → Subahu
nodes.era: Gens 5-94 (Pargiter Ch. IX p. 101; Ch. XIII pp. 153-155)
nodes.role: Ancient Sacred Kingdom of Varanasi & Origin of Ayurveda
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 101, 145-155
nodes.notes: Ayu's son Kshatravriddha founded Kasi (Varanasi); King Dhanvantari is revered as the founder of Ayurvedic medicine; Divodasa II & Pratardana (Gen 41) broke Haihaya dominance alongside Sagara of Ayodhya!

nodes.name: Haihaya Dynasty (Yadu → Sahasrajit): Haihaya → Mahishmant (Mahishmati) → Bhadrashrenya → Kritavirya → Emperor Kartavirya Arjuna → Jayadhvaja → Talajanghas (5 Clans)
nodes.role: Central Indian Narmada Empire & Nemesis of Parashurama & Sagara
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102, 144-146, 153-156
nodes.notes: Kartavirya Arjuna (Gen 31, thousand-armed emperor of Mahishmati) captured Ravana, raided Kasi and Ayodhya, and clashed fatally with Bhargava Parashurama; his descendants the 5 Talajangha clans (Vitihotras, Bhojas, Avantis, Sharyatas, Tundikeras) were finally crushed by Sagara (Gen 41).

nodes.name: Yadava Main Line (Kroshtu → Satvata): Shashabindu → Jyamagha → Vidarbha (Cedi & Kratha-Bhima) → Madhu → Satvata → Andhaka (Kukura → Ugrasena → Kamsa) & Vrishni (Shura → Vasudeva → Krishna → Samba & Vajra)
nodes.role: Complete Yadava Pedigree from Yadu to Krishna, Kamsa & Surviving Heir Vajra
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 102-107, 144-148, 284
nodes.notes: Unites ALL Yadava branches: Shashabindu (Gen 20), Jyamagha -> Vidarbha (founder of Vidarbha & Cedi), Madhu (eponym of Mathura/Madhava), Satvata -> Andhaka (Ugrasena -> King Kamsa; Kritavarman) & Vrishni (Devamidhusha -> Shura -> Vasudeva & Kunti -> Krishna, Balarama, Satyaki; grandson Vajra installed at Indraprastha!).

nodes.name: Druhyus (Gandhara → Pracetas — Northward Migration Beyond India!) & Turvasus (Marutta → Adopted Dushyanta → Pandya, Kerala & Chola)
nodes.role: Northwest (Gandhara/Central Asia) & South Indian (Tamil) Aila Bridges
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108, 144, 146
nodes.notes: Druhyu's descendant Gandhara gave his name to Gandhara (NW Pakistan/Afghanistan); Pracetas's 100 sons migrated north beyond the Himalayas into mleccha lands! Turvasu's line merged into the Pauravas via Marutta's adoption of Dushyanta, with southern Puranic tradition deriving Pandya, Kerala, and Chola from it.

nodes.name: Anavas (Anu's Two Empires): NW Panjab (Ushinara → King Shibi → Kekaya, Madra, Sauvira) & East Bihar (Titikshu → Bali → Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Pundra, Suhma → Lomapada → King Karna!)
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 108-109, 145-149
nodes.notes: Mahamanas split the Anavas: Ushinara -> famously compassionate King Shibi (and Kekaya/Madra, mothers of Bharata & Nakula/Sahadeva!); Titikshu -> King Bali -> 5 sons founding Anga, Vanga (Bengal!), Kalinga (Odisha!), Pundra & Suhma -> Lomapada (friend of Dasharatha) -> Mahabharata hero Karna -> Vrishasena!

nodes.name: North & South Panchalas (Ajamidha → Nila & Brihadvasu): Mudgala → Divodasa (Atithigva) → King Sudas (Battle of the Ten Kings!) → Drupada → Draupadi & Dhrishtadyumna (+ Drona & Ashvatthama)
nodes.role: Rigvedic Battle of Ten Kings Hero Sudas & Panchala Allies of the Pandavas
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 115-117, 146-148
Rigveda VII.18
nodes.notes: Ajamidha's son Nila founded North Panchala (Ahicchattra): Bhrmyashva's 5 sons ('Panchalas') -> Mudgala -> Vadhryashva -> Divodasa (sister Ahalya!) -> King Sudas (victor of the Rigvedic Dasharajna / Battle of Ten Kings against Samvarana & the Ten Tribes!) -> Drupada (father of Draupadi & Dhrishtadyumna, rival of Guru Drona!).

nodes.name: Cedi & Magadha (Kuru → Sudhanvan → Vasu Uparichara): Brihadratha → Jarasandha → Sahadeva → Somadhi (Magadha) & Damaghosha → Shishupala (Cedi)
nodes.role: First Historical Dynasty of Magadha (Barhadrathas) & Cedi
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 118-119, 149
nodes.notes: Kuru's son Sudhanvan's descendant Emperor Vasu Caidyoparichara conquered Cedi & Magadha; his eldest son Brihadratha founded the Barhadratha Dynasty of Magadha -> Emperor Jarasandha (slain by Bhima!) -> Sahadeva -> Somadhi (start of the 22 post-battle Barhadratha kings!).

nodes.name: Post-Mahabharata Kurus (Gens 96–105+): Parikshit II → Janamejaya III → Shatanika → Adhisimakrishna (c. 850 BCE) → Nicakshu (Moved Capital to Kaushambi!) → King Udayana of Vatsa
nodes.era: c. 950-500 BCE (Pargiter Ch. XXIV p. 285; Ch. XXVII p. 330)
nodes.role: Continuation of the Pandava/Kuru Royal Line After Hastinapura Flood
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 285, 330
nodes.notes: When the Ganges washed away Hastinapura c. 820 BCE, Arjuna's 6th-generation descendant Nicakshu moved the Kuru capital to Kaushambi in Vatsa — culminating in famed King Udayana of Vatsa, contemporary of Gautama Buddha!

nodes.name: Bhargavas (Bhrigu → Shukra, Cyavana, Urva → Richika → Jamadagni → Parashurama, Valmiki) & Angirasas (Atharvan → Brihaspati → Bharadvaja → Drona → Ashvatthama; Dirghatamas → Gautama → Kripa; Kanvas)
nodes.role: Complete Genealogies of the Bhargava, Angirasa & Kanva Seers
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 191-202, 218-227
nodes.notes: Synchronizes every great Vedic & Epic sage with the 95-generation royal table: Cyavana (Gen 2), Shukra (Gen 5), Richika/Jamadagni/Parashurama (Gens 31-33), Atharvan/Brihaspati/Dirghatamas/Bharadvaja (Gens 38-41), Valmiki (Gen 64, author of Ramayana!), and Bharadvaja -> Guru Drona -> Ashvatthama (Gens 92-94).

nodes.name: Vasishthas (Vasishtha → Shakti → Parashara → Vyasa → Shuka), Atreyas (Datta & Durvasas), Kashyapas (Kanva, Rishyashringa) & Agastya (+ Lopamudra)
nodes.era: Gens 1-94 (Pargiter Ch. XVIII, XX, XXII, pp. 203-242)
nodes.role: Complete Pedigrees of Vyasa, Durvasas, Rishyashringa & Agastya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 203-242
nodes.notes: Traces the genuine Vasishtha pedigree (Gen 68 Vasishtha with Sudas -> Shakti -> Parashara -> Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa [Gen 92, compiler of Vedas & Mahabharata!] -> Shuka), Atreya sages Datta & Durvasas (Gen 31), Kashyapa foster-father Kanva (of Shakuntala) & Rishyashringa, and Agastya (+ Lopamudra of Vidarbha, Gen 42).

nodes.name: Historical Magadha Empires: Barhadrathas (22 Kings) → Pradyotas (5 Kings) → Haryanka/Shishunaga (King Bimbisara & Ajatashatru — Patrons of Buddha!) → 9 Nandas (Mahapadma Nanda)
nodes.role: Bridge from Mahabharata Magadha to Buddha, Alexander & Chandragupta Maurya
sources: Pargiter Ancient Indian Historical Tradition pp. 179-182, 286-287
nodes.notes: Pargiter's critical chronology: 22 Barhadrathas (c. 950-619 BCE) -> 5 Pradyotas -> Shishunaga/Haryanka (Bimbisara & Ajatashatru, contemporaries of Buddha c. 487 BCE!) -> Mahapadma Nanda & 8 sons (exterminated all 10 ancient Kshatriya kingdoms c. 382 BCE, creating the vast empire seized by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE!).

nodes.name: Gupta Empire (Golden Age of India): Sri Gupta → Chandragupta I (+ Kumaradevi Licchavi) → Samudragupta → Chandragupta II Vikramaditya → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta
nodes.role: Classical Golden Age of Sanskrit, Astronomy (Aryabhata) & Nalanda
sources: Allahabad Pillar Inscription
Vishnu Purana IV.24
nodes.notes: Chandragupta I married Licchavi princess Kumaradevi (of ancient Vaisali!), launching India's Golden Age under Samudragupta & Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (court of Kalidasa!).
